assembly_stair.name: Assembly Stair
assembly_stair.description: Twelve parts, three objects, and the word `assembly` doing three different jobs that only a part count can tell apart. A 0.68 m bench plate carries the same twelve pieces in every one of twenty-one cells - four 0.26 x 0.030 x 0.13 m decks, four 0.060 x 0.26 x 0.060 m posts, four 0.26 x 0.024 x 0.024 m ties - and nothing about them changes but where they go. Three artifacts declare an axis called assembly and spend eleven words between them, of which exactly ONE is shared: full. Counted in meshes at their own defaults, cube_staircase runs 6, 11, 13, 26 - strictly additive, strictly nested, and its non-full values genuinely OMIT parts rather than highlighting them. recursive_table runs 13, 5, 5, 9 - non-monotone and not nested, because its step 2 destroys nine cells to make one slab and its step 3 adds no mesh at all. bricoleur_golem runs 6, 6, 6, 6 - constant, same parts, only the joinery. So the axis holds a decomposition, a derivation and a degree, and the part count is what separates them: a decomposition draws a subset, a derivation replaces parts, a degree always draws the whole set. Here treads draws 4 of 12, legs 4, cells 8, slab 4 parts as ONE mesh, and full, lashed and heap all draw 12 - so treads + legs = cells and cells + ties = full, exactly, while the two degree values refuse to enter the ledger. Crossed against three objects the check comes back sharp: the same decomposition word on two different objects is 42-43 percent apart, and heap is 0.000 percent apart, because a pile does not know what the parts were going to be. Nothing animates, nothing is random, nothing bakes on a worker thread.
dev_themes: one word doing the work of three ladders
interactions: count the meshes at each assembly value and read the ledger off the frames: treads 4, legs 4, cells 8, slab 4 parts as one mesh, full 12, lashed 12, heap 12 - and notice that no value below twelve is a degree and no degree is below twelve

walk the object axis at assembly=slab: the same instruction, fuse the four decks into their bounding box, gives a tabletop you can barely tell from four quadrants (0.52 percent), a slightly filled trunk on the figure (3.28), and a solid block on the stair (42.96) - a merge is invisible exactly when the parts were already flush
stand at assembly=slab, object=stair and read cube_staircase's truth line back off the frame: the staircase un-subdivided is the cube it was cut from

walk the object axis at assembly=heap and look for the difference: there is none, to the byte, because bricoleur_golem's heap table never consults the body plan - the object axis is worth 43 percent everywhere else and nothing here
put cells against full on any object: the whole difference is four 0.024 m ties, about 6 percent, which is how little the bracing is worth in a photograph and how much it is worth to the object
assembly_stair.capacity: SEE that `assembly` is one word carrying three different ladders - a decomposition that grows by subsets, a derivation that replaces its parts, and a degree that never shows fewer than all of them - and that the part count is the only thing in a still that tells them apart

spatial_needs.footprint_note: THE STAGE IS THE FOOTPRINT and it is drawn before either axis is consulted: a 0.68 x 0.68 m plate and an invisible layers = 0 anchor of 0.68 x 0.58 x 0.68 centred at y 0.29. The drawn object runs 0.412 x 0.545 x 0.520 m at full/stair, 0.530 x 0.290 x 0.290 at full/table, 0.380 x 0.458 x 0.260 at full/figure, down to 0.530 x 0.030 x 0.270 at treads/table, and the heap spreads widest and flattest at 0.613 x 0.188 x 0.546 - a 4.5x spread in the diagonal - while the world box stays 0.68 x 0.58 x 0.68 in all twenty-one cells. That is why the anchor exists: without it every cell would be photographed at its own focal length and every measured pair would be reporting zoom. layout=ladder stands all three objects in a row at 0.90 m pitch, about 2.3 m wide, and is a design view rather than a map placement.

measurements.source: computed_from_geometry in a Python replica built from the same constants and the same four position tables; no Godot was run. The box is the layers = 0 ANCHOR and nothing else, which is what makes it identical in all twenty-one variants by construction. Every drawn part is inside it with margin: the tallest thing in any cell is the top baluster at y 0.570 (lashed/stair) against a 0.58 ceiling, and the widest is the heap at x -0.325 to 0.288 against a +-0.34 plate.

dna.default: assembly=full, object=stair. `full` is the default because it is the shipped default of BOTH members that carry a decomposition - cube_staircase's and recursive_table's - and the only word the two vocabularies share, and because a decomposition's partial values are partial WITH RESPECT TO it, so the assembled object is the honest reference. `stair` is the default because cube_staircase is the member that lent the axis its terminal value first and because it is the token's own name. NOTE WHAT THIS COSTS AND DOES NOT COST: the default cell is the fullest, busiest tile in the sheet, which would normally be a bad place to solve framing - except that framing here is set by the layers = 0 anchor and the anchor is identical in every variant, so the camera distance is the same whichever cell is measured.
dna.note:
WHAT THE VALUES MEAN, which member each came from, whether it is a DECOMPOSITION or a DEGREE, and HOW MANY OF THE TWELVE PARTS IT DRAWS. THE FAMILY FIRST, as a census before it is an argument: `assembly` is declared by three artifacts spending ELEVEN words between them, and exactly ONE word appears in two lists. cube_staircase says treads | steps | stringers | full; recursive_table says cells | slab | legs | full; bricoleur_golem says figure | lashed | cairn | heap. The shared word is `full`, and that it is the ONLY shared word is the finding this bench is built on.

THE THING THE CODE SAYS THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT, and it is a correction rather than a refinement. The brief said the axis holds TWO things: a decomposition (which parts are shown) and a degree (how organised the whole set is). Counted in meshes at each member's shipped defaults, THE CODE SAYS THREE.

  cube_staircase   treads 6 -> steps 11 -> stringers 13 -> full 26 meshes at step_count=6. STRICTLY ADDITIVE AND STRICTLY NESTED. And the brief's own question - do the non-`full` values OMIT parts or merely HIGHLIGHT them - has a flat answer: THEY OMIT. _shows_risers, _shows_stringers and _shows_handrail return false and _create_part is never called, so the omitted parts do not exist in the tree at all; there is no dimming, no ghosting, no alpha. treads is a subset of steps is a subset of stringers is a subset of full. A TRUE DECOMPOSITION. One nuance the count exposes and the words hide: the rungs are CUMULATIVE PREFIXES, not a parts list. `steps` is treads-plus-risers, not risers alone. Nobody in this family ever shows a sub-assembly BY ITSELF except at the first rung.

  recursive_table  cells 13 -> slab 5 -> legs 5 -> full 9 meshes at keep=corners. NON-MONOTONE AND NOT NESTED, which makes it something else wearing the same word. Step 2 DESTROYS nine tabletop cells and creates one slab, so the count FALLS by eight; step 3 adds nothing whatever - it rewrites box.size.x/z/y and position.y on four cells already standing and recolours them, 5 meshes before and 5 after; only step 4 adds (+4 apron). So `cells` is NOT a subset of `full`: the nine cells it shows have been queue_free'd by the time `full` exists. That is a DERIVATION - a sequence of states - and a derivation is not a decomposition, however identical the vocabulary looks.

  bricoleur_golem  figure 6 -> lashed 6 -> cairn 6 -> heap 6. CONSTANT. All four values run _build_random_part(i) for i in 0..5; only which of four literal position arrays is read, and whether a cant is applied, changes. Its own comment states the law: "Same six parts, same six sizes - only the joinery changes." A DEGREE.

SO THE PART COUNT IS THE INSTRUMENT, and it is why the brief's demand to state it is the whole experiment rather than bookkeeping. A DECOMPOSITION draws a SUBSET and its count rises to the terminal value. A DERIVATION's count falls and rises, because parts are REPLACED rather than added. A DEGREE always draws the WHOLE SET and never fewer - which is the definition, and the reason no count can rank two degree values against each other.

AND WHY bricoleur_golem HAS NO `full`, sharpened against the brief. The brief said: because a heap is not a partial assembly, it is a different arrangement of the complete set. True, and not the reason. The reason is that `figure` IS its full - the complete set in its intended arrangement, shipped as the default, its own comment calling it "the shipped six-slot humanoid". The family does not lack a terminal value. It has one, named with a degree word instead of a completeness word, which is exactly what you would expect of a vocabulary that never counts.

WHAT THIS BENCH BUILDS. TWELVE PARTS, three groups of four, THE SAME TWELVE IN ALL TWENTY-ONE CELLS - same sizes, same colours, same order, only the placement changes. That law is bricoleur_golem's, adopted verbatim, and without it the count is not an instrument. 4 DECKS 0.26 x 0.030 x 0.13, the horizontal plates, in cube_staircase's step_color. 4 POSTS 0.060 x 0.26 x 0.060, the vertical members, in recursive_table's leg colour. 4 TIES 0.26 x 0.024 x 0.024, the thin braces added last, in cube_staircase's rail_color.

ASSEMBLY, seven values. THE LEDGER IS EXACT AND IT IS THE CLAIM: treads(4) + legs(4) = cells(8) by construction, and cells(8) + the 4 ties = full(12). The decomposition values form an additive ledger over the twelve. THE TWO DEGREE VALUES DO NOT ENTER IT - both draw 12, which is what makes them degrees.

  cells - recursive_table. DECOMPOSITION. 8 OF 12 DRAWN (4 decks + 4 posts; the ties are absent). Its step 1: the kept parts standing as separate blocks before anything is merged or braced. The half of its meaning this bench DECLINES is in `declines` - its cells are also un-stretched, and these parts have fixed sizes so there is no stretch to undo.

  treads - cube_staircase, and the only word it lends. DECOMPOSITION. 4 OF 12 DRAWN (the deck group alone). What the diagonal subdivision yields before anything is closed, walled or railed.

  slab - recursive_table. DECOMPOSITION, and the derivation's signature. 4 PARTS ACCOUNTED, 1 MESH DRAWN. THE ONLY VALUE IN THE SHEET WHERE PART COUNT AND MESH COUNT DISAGREE, and that disagreement is the whole tell: a merge is the move that makes a ladder stop being a decomposition. The box is the world AABB of the four deck parts as this object places them, so the merge costs exactly what the parts' separation costs. On the table that is two 0.010 m seams and almost nothing. On the stair it is 0.285 m of rise, and the answer is A SOLID BLOCK - which is cube_staircase's own truth line handed back: a staircase is a cube that learned to subdivide itself along its own diagonal, so un-subdividing it returns the cube.

  legs - recursive_table. DECOMPOSITION. 4 OF 12 DRAWN (the post group alone). On the stair these are balusters standing on treads that are not drawn, so they hang in the air - which is honest and is the same condition recursive_table's own `cells` is in.

  full - BOTH first members, the ONLY word they share, and both members' shipped default. DECOMPOSITION terminal. 12 OF 12 DRAWN, every part in its place. AND IT IS NOT THE BANNED ALL-RUNGS VALUE, which is worth saying plainly because it looks like one. The banned thing puts every VALUE of an axis into a single cell, so every other value becomes a subset of that cell, the sweep unions the AABB across a two-and-a-half-metre row, and nothing can be compared with anything. `full` puts every PART of ONE object into a cell at ONE value of ONE axis. Its extent is the object's own. It is what a decomposition vocabulary is FOR - the assembled thing the partial values are partial with respect to - and a decomposition without it has no referent. The actually-banned value lives in `layout` below, outside both axes, pinned by the fixture.

  lashed - bricoleur_golem. DEGREE. 12 OF 12 DRAWN. Its second rung, which its own comment glosses as keeping the plan but letting the joints show, canted and gapped. Here every part takes a constant displacement (about 0.013 m) and a constant cant (up to 0.26 rad, against the member's randf_range(-0.45, 0.45)) on top of the object's own placement. OBJECT-AWARE: it loosens THIS object's plan, so it is a different picture on each of the three.

  heap - bricoleur_golem. DEGREE. 12 OF 12 DRAWN. Its last rung: the pile that has not yet been made into anything. Its HEAP_POSITIONS is a literal array CONSULTED INSTEAD OF the body plan rather than derived from it, so its heap is the same heap whatever the golem was. That is kept here exactly, which makes `heap` identical across all three objects - the sheet's designed null and half its argument.

OBJECT, three values, one per member, and THIS AXIS IS THE CHECK. A decomposition value should mean the same thing on all three objects (show me the deck group) and a degree value should mean the same thing too and yet produce a very different picture.

  stair - cube_staircase. Decks ascend along +Z at 0.085 rise over 0.130 run; posts stand on the treads as balusters at x = -0.215 (its rail_offset is -0.52 * stair_size, outside the stair, on ONE side only, and that asymmetry is its, not this bench's); ties are two pitched side rails per flank at x = +-0.155, its stringer and handrail run. Extent 0.412 x 0.545 x 0.520 m at `full`.
  table - recursive_table. Decks are four quadrants of one top; posts are corner legs at +-0.177 x and +-0.115 z, which is its 3x3 corner-cell rule (+-1/3 of the top's span) to the millimetre; ties are the apron ring, INSET from the legs as its own numbers are (apron table_size*0.65 against a leg reach of table_size*0.70). Extent 0.530 x 0.290 x 0.290 m at `full`.
  figure - bricoleur_golem. Four decks stack as a trunk; two posts are legs and two are arms; three ties are bands across chest, shoulders and hips and one lies across the crown. Extent 0.380 x 0.458 x 0.260 m at `full`.

AND WHERE THE CHECK FAILS, said rather than invented around. IS `treads` MEANINGLESS ON A TABLE? Not meaningless - PARTIAL, and the part that survives is the smaller half. As a GEOMETRIC role it transfers exactly: it names the horizontal plates, and they exist on all three objects. As a FUNCTIONAL word it does not transfer at all. A tread is the surface you put your foot on, one of an ascending series. A tabletop is horizontal and you do not stand on it. A torso plate is horizontal and is not a surface at all. So the word carries WHICH PARTS and drops WHAT THEY ARE FOR - and this bench uses only the first half, and says so here rather than pretending a table has treads. THE FAMILY ALREADY KNEW: recursive_table's own header records that it imported `assembly` and its terminal value `full` from one folder over and then substituted cells/slab/legs, "the same question with this object's own part names". That renaming IS the failure of transfer, performed by the family and never named by it.

THE THESIS SOMEONE COULD DISAGREE WITH: A DECOMPOSITION VOCABULARY DOES NOT TRAVEL BETWEEN OBJECTS; ONLY ITS TERMINAL VALUE DOES. Two members share this axis and share exactly one word, and that word is the one that names a QUANTITY OF COMPLETION rather than a part. A degree vocabulary travels intact, because degree of order is a fact about arrangement and any set of parts can be more or less arranged - which is why bricoleur_golem's four words would survive being handed to a staircase and cube_staircase's four would not survive being handed to a golem. Measured on the replica: at every decomposition value the same word on two different objects is 42.4 to 43.3 percent apart, and at `heap` it is 0.000 percent. The object axis is worth about 43 percent to a decomposition and exactly nothing to a degree at minimum order. THE DISAGREEMENT AVAILABLE, and it is fair: a reader can say the bench engineered that zero by copying bricoleur_golem's constant heap table, and it did. The answer is that the constant table is the member's own design decision and the finding is about what that decision MEANS - a vocabulary that does not consult the object cannot be a vocabulary about the object.

WHAT THE MERGE COSTS, AND IT IS THE CROSS-AXIS NUMBER. `treads` against `slab` is the same instruction on all three objects - fuse the four deck parts into their bounding box - and it measures 0.52 percent on the table, 3.28 percent on the figure and 42.96 percent on the stair. Same operation, same parts, two orders of magnitude. A MERGE IS INVISIBLE EXACTLY WHEN THE PARTS WERE ALREADY FLUSH, and recursive_table's step 2 looks like a large change in its own source mostly because its nine cells are table_size*0.4 TALL and its slab is table_size*0.04 thin - it flattens as well as fusing, and the flattening is doing most of the work. See `declines`.

HOW THE SHEET IS PROTECTED FROM THE COLOUR TRAP. The critic measures luminance and has a separate per-channel rescue, so a pair separated only by hue reads as a twin in greyscale. NOTHING HERE IS SEPARATED BY HUE. The three part colours are fixed per GROUP and never per value or per object, so no pair of cells differs in colour without also differing in which parts are present or where they are. If the colour-only rescue ever fires on this sheet it is reporting a fault, not a rescue.

predicted_degeneracy.pair: treads against slab, on the table object
predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic:
Rasterised BEFORE ANY CAPTURE in the critic's own currency: the twelve parts, the plate and the anchor rebuilt in Python from the same constants and the same four position tables, projected through capture_config_sweep's camera (FOV 34, PAD 1.9, yaw 0.62, pitch -0.26, 760 x 760, framing 0.60 on the union AABB, which is the ANCHOR at 0.68 x 0.58 x 0.68 and therefore identical in all twenty-one cells), z-buffered with the default rig's key at (-42, -35) energy 1.25, fill at (-20, 130) energy 0.45 and ambient (0.62, 0.65, 0.72) at 0.55, tonemapped, sRGB out - then run through artifact_dna_critic's pipeline unchanged: subject bbox from pixel (3,3), crop to the union of the two frames' subject boxes, neutralise each frame's own corner, grey, resize 160 x 160, mean of the hottest 5 percent.

THE CONTEXT IS THE `table` OBJECT AND THE RANKING IS COMPUTED INSIDE IT. All twenty-one pairs at object=table, focus percent, in order: treads-slab 0.52, cells-full 6.03, full-lashed 35.39, cells-lashed 36.12, slab-full 40.53, treads-full 40.53, cells-slab 40.85, cells-treads 40.86, treads-lashed 42.23, slab-lashed 42.24, legs-heap 42.95, legs-lashed 42.97, legs-full 43.21, cells-legs 43.21, slab-legs 43.27, treads-legs 43.27, full-heap 43.34, cells-heap 43.38, slab-heap 43.42, treads-heap 43.43, lashed-heap 43.52. IT IS A SINGLE PAIR, not a cluster: the runner-up is 11.7x further away.

WHY THAT PAIR, WITH THE NUMBERS. At object=table the four decks are coplanar quadrants of one top, laid on a 0.27 x 0.14 m pitch with 0.26 x 0.13 m plates, so the only thing between them is a 0.010 m seam cross. `slab` replaces the four with one box spanning their union - the same outline, the same thickness, the same height - so the ENTIRE difference between the two frames is that cross. Its world area is 0.010 x 0.270 + 0.010 x 0.530 - 0.010 x 0.010 = 0.00790 m2. It lies on a horizontal face read at 0.26 rad of elevation, so its screen-plane area is 0.00790 x sin(0.26) = 0.00203 m2 against a frame of 1.2803 x 1.2803 = 1.6392 m2, i.e. 0.124 percent of frame. Measured on the replica: 851 pixels of 577600 differ by more than 4 grey levels = 0.147 percent, the extra 0.023 being the side walls of the gap, which the merge also removes.

AND THEN THE CRITIC'S ARITHMETIC, WHICH IS WHERE THE NUMBER ACTUALLY COMES FROM. The crop is the subject box, 545 x 336 px = 31.7 percent of frame, resized to 160 x 160 = 25600 samples. Only 305 of those 25600 carry any change at all. The hottest-5-percent window is 1280 samples, SO THE WINDOW IS ONLY 24 PERCENT FULL and the rest of it is zeros. THIS IS THE ONE PAIR IN THE SHEET WHERE THE WINDOW DOES NOT SATURATE, which means the number is a measure of AREA and not of contrast: mean over the window = 1.32 of 255 = 0.517 percent. It also gives a ceiling. If the real render's shadows and AO widen the seam until the window fills, the same contrasts give 1280/305 x 0.517 = 2.17 percent; to exceed that, the seam must photograph DARKER than the replica's unlit gap, which shadow mapping and SSAO can plausibly do. So the honest expectation band is 0.52 to about 3.5 percent.

THE PREDICTION IS A FLOOR, NOT A FORECAST. The replica has one key, one fill, flat shading, no shadows, no AO, no antialiasing; every prior prediction in this corpus under-read by 1.5x to 6.7x. IF THE SWEEP COMES BACK BELOW 0.517 PERCENT ON THE NAMED PAIR, STOP AND INVESTIGATE THE HARNESS BEFORE THE DESIGN: (a) tools/check_dna_declarations.py - a value the code cannot reach falls back to the default and prints identical tiles; (b) _rejects.json - both exports are String enums and Object.set() on a typed property of the wrong type is refused in SILENCE; (c) whether the sheet was captured with --max=21, because at build_dna_gallery's default cap of 9 the 7 x 3 cross product is trimmed from the tail of the LATER axis and `object` collapses to [stair] alone, which deletes all three designed nulls, the whole cross-object claim, and the registered pair's context.

THE PAIR AT REAL RISK IS NOT THIS ONE. `cells` against `full` measures 6.03 / 6.26 / 7.34 percent across the three objects, and that difference is FOUR THIN TIES - 0.024 m bars, two of which are edge-on or behind a leg at yaw 0.62 on the table. If it lands under 3 percent the finding is that the tie group is not photographable from the canonical standpoint, which is an ANAMORPHIC candidate and NOT a reason to redesign the axis: run probe_anamorphic.py before believing any dead verdict about it.

designed_nulls.why: IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AND IT IS HALF THE THESIS, not a spare check. `heap` reads HEAP_POS, a literal table that never looks at the object - which is bricoleur_golem's own construction, where HEAP_POSITIONS is consulted INSTEAD OF the body plan rather than derived from it. Twelve parts, same sizes, same colours, same places. So a degree value at minimum order cannot see the object axis at all, while the same axis is worth 43.27 percent between treads/stair and treads/table. Predicted 0.000 percent focus and 0.000 percent frame, confirmed at 0.0000 / 0.0000 on the replica; anything above 1 percent is render noise or an unsettled first tile, and anything above 2 percent means `object` is reaching the heap table.

The second pair, registered separately because a null that held for one pair and broke for another would mean the object is reaching the pile somewhere it must not. figure is the object whose own arrangement is furthest from a heap - a standing trunk with limbs, 0.380 x 0.458 x 0.260 against the pile's 0.613 x 0.188 x 0.546 - and at `heap` it is the same photograph as a table, which is the strongest single statement the sheet makes about what a degree word forgets.

The third pair, and the one that closes the triangle. All three must be 0.00 together; two zeros and one non-zero is arithmetically impossible for identical images and would be a fact about the harness rather than about the artifact - most likely an unsettled first tile, which is why the critic neutralises each frame's own corner before measuring.

dna.designed_nulls_why: THREE NULLS, ONE FACT, AND IT IS HALF THE THESIS. `heap` is the same photograph on all three objects because bricoleur_golem's HEAP_POSITIONS is a literal array consulted INSTEAD OF the body plan - the pile does not know what the parts were going to be - and that is reproduced here exactly. So the `object` axis, which is worth 42.4 to 43.3 percent at every other value of `assembly`, is worth 0.000 percent here. A DEGREE AT MINIMUM ORDER ERASES THE OBJECT; a decomposition never can, because a decomposition value names parts and parts are placed by the object. The three pairs are registered SEPARATELY and must all be 0.00 together: two zeros and one non-zero is arithmetically impossible for identical images and would be a fact about the harness rather than about the artifact - most likely an unsettled first tile, which is why the critic neutralises each frame's own corner. THE TEMPTING FOURTH IS `treads` AGAINST `slab` ON THE TABLE, and it is deliberately NOT a null: the 0.010 m seam cross is real geometry and 0.517 percent is the pre-registered closest pair. If any of the three zeros comes back above 1 percent, nothing else in this sheet can be believed.
dna.fixture_why: The bench can stand all three objects in a row (layout=ladder, 0.90 m pitch, about 2.3 m wide) but the SWEEP must see one at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so a three-wide row in the same spec would frame every single cell against two and a half metres and photograph the 0.010 m seam that carries the registered prediction as nothing at all. layout is an export and not an axis, and it ships at single, so the fixture is a belt over braces. WHAT IS NOT FIXTURED, AND WHY NOTHING NEEDS TO BE: there is no clock and no random number here. The whole object is built synchronously inside _ready from four constant position tables - no _process, no Timer, no tween, no randf, no noise, no NoiseTexture2D. That matters because ALL THREE SOURCES ARE NOISY: cube_staircase ships show_construction = true and its own registry records that a sweep must pin it false or photograph a half-built staircase AND place its one fixed camera on a single tread; recursive_table ships show_animation = true and runs four steps at 0.4 s; bricoleur_golem needed a part_seed export to stop a sweep photographing four different golems.
dna.kin: The three sources are the kin and the relation is unusually literal: two of them are siblings in the same folder (algorithms/fractals/cubesubdivision) and the third is a hazard creature in commons/hazards, and this bench is the only place the two lineages meet. cube_staircase's truth line is that a staircase is a cube that learned to subdivide itself along its own diagonal - which this bench photographs directly at assembly=slab, object=stair, where merging the four treads returns the block. recursive_table's is that a table is a cube that kept its top layer and four corners, everything else being excess; its own header is the source of this bench's thesis, because it records the moment the vocabulary failed to transfer and renamed itself. bricoleur_golem's is that the bricoleur does not design, it discovers what available parts want to become - and it is the member that supplies both the degree words and the construction (fixed parts, literal position tables) that the other two made necessary. A room holding this bench beside cube_staircase is saying the same sentence twice about a stair; a room holding it beside bricoleur_golem is asking whether a parts list and a pile are the same kind of statement. ON THE VALUE SIDE this is the corpus's WIDEST shared axis name with the NARROWEST shared vocabulary: three artifacts, eleven words, one word in common.
declines: THE BRIEF'S ARGUMENT, CORRECTED FROM THE CODE, and it is the biggest change. The brief said the axis holds TWO things - a decomposition and a degree - and that cube_staircase and recursive_table are the same idea. THE COUNT SAYS THEY ARE NOT. cube_staircase is strictly additive and strictly nested (6, 11, 13, 26 meshes; every value a subset of full). recursive_table is non-monotone and NOT nested (13, 5, 5, 9 meshes): its step 2 destroys nine cells to make one slab, its step 3 adds no mesh at all and merely rewrites box.size and position.y on four cells already standing, and its `cells` value shows nine objects that do not exist at `full`. That is a DERIVATION, a sequence of states, not a decomposition, a parts list. So the axis holds THREE things, and the discriminator is the part count: a subset that grows, a set that is replaced, and a set that is never smaller.

THE BRIEF'S QUESTION ABOUT cube_staircase, ANSWERED FLATLY. It asked whether the non-`full` values really omit parts or merely highlight them, because those are different claims. THEY OMIT: _shows_risers / _shows_stringers / _shows_handrail gate the calls, _create_part is never reached, and the part is not in the tree. No dimming, no alpha, no ghost. But the same reading turns up something the brief assumed away - the rungs are CUMULATIVE PREFIXES, not a parts list. `steps` is treads-plus-risers, not risers alone; `stringers` is all of that plus the side walls. Nowhere in either member does a value show ONE sub-assembly by itself except at the first rung. This bench keeps the prefix reading for `cells` and `full` and breaks it for `treads` and `legs`, which are single groups shown alone - a deliberate deviation, so that treads(4) + legs(4) = cells(8) is a checkable ledger rather than an assertion.

`steps` from cube_staircase and `cairn` from bricoleur_golem, both real values, both declined for sheet width. `steps` is treads-plus-risers, and this bench has no riser group: a riser is a thin vertical plate closing the gap under a tread, and building one would need a FOURTH part group that has no meaning on a table or a figure, which is the transfer failure this bench is about rather than a thing it should smuggle in. `cairn` is the degree between `lashed` and `heap` - stacking, anatomy abandoned but verticality kept - and it is the first value to add if the axis ever wants an eighth. Seven values against three objects is already 21 cells.

`figure` FROM bricoleur_golem AS AN EIGHTH VALUE, and this is the designed null the brief named, declined on arithmetic rather than on principle. `figure` is the complete set in the object's intended arrangement, which is precisely what `full` is; a degree value at maximum order and a decomposition value at completion are THE SAME ARRANGEMENT OF THE SAME TWELVE PARTS. Building it would put three cells in the sheet that are 0.00 percent from three cells already there, and the sheet is 21 cells wide. The identity is registered as arithmetic here instead: the degree ladder's top rung is the decomposition ladder's terminal value, which is why bricoleur_golem needs no `full` and why `full` is the one word two vocabularies could share.

THE FLATTENING HALF OF recursive_table's `slab`, and this one is a real weakening. Its _step_2_shape_tabletop does TWO things: it fuses nine cells into one, and it thins them from table_size * 0.4 to table_size * 0.04, a ten-fold flattening. This bench's decks are already 0.030 m plates, so there is nothing to flatten and `slab` is a fusion only. Most of what a reader sees at that step in the source is therefore the half not built here. Building it would have meant a deck group whose thickness is a function of the assembly value, which breaks the fixed-size law that makes the part count legible and makes `heap` object-blind - and that law is worth more than the flattening.

THE UN-STRETCHED HALF OF recursive_table's `cells`. Its cells are also PRE-TRANSFORM: the leg cells float in the lower layer and have not yet been extended to the floor. Here the posts have fixed sizes and there is no stretch to undo, so `cells` is full-minus-ties and nothing more. The floating condition still appears in the sheet, at `legs` on the stair, where four balusters stand on treads that are not drawn.

`step_count` from cube_staircase and `keep` from recursive_table as a third axis. Both are real and both are the member's OTHER question - how finely the diagonal is discretised, and which cells of the subdivision survive - and neither is about how much of the object is standing. A bench that swept one of them beside `assembly` would be answering two questions in one sheet and could not attribute either. `salvage` from bricoleur_golem is declined for a second reason as well: it is about what the parts are MADE OF, and this bench's twelve parts are fixed by construction, so a salvage axis here would have nothing to vary.

ANIMATION, AND EVERY RATE AND DELAY. All three members animate their assembly: cube_staircase ships show_construction = true and builds one part every 0.3 s, recursive_table ships show_animation = true and runs four steps at 0.4 s, bricoleur_golem scatters and re-snaps over rebuild_time. NONE OF IT IS IN A STILL, and cube_staircase's registry already records the consequence: its sweep MUST pin show_construction = false or capture_config_sweep's 1.1 s settle photographs a half-built staircase and, worse, places its one fixed camera on a single tread. This bench has no clock at all - no _process, no Timer, no tween - so there is nothing to pin and no way for the shutter to catch it mid-build.

RANDOMNESS, INCLUDING A SEEDED ONE. bricoleur_golem needed a part_seed export because the shipped global randf() made every render a different golem. This bench goes one step further and has no generator: `lashed` and `heap` are constant tables, which is stronger than a seed because a seed is only as reproducible as the NUMBER OF DRAWS TAKEN BEFORE IT - the trap that member guards against by taking three cant draws whether or not the value uses them, so that the stream stays aligned across assembly values. A table cannot desynchronise.

A BIGGER OBJECT IN THE FRAME. Everything could be scaled up and every pair would read hotter, but the plate's margin is what keeps the heap's 0.613 m spread inside the anchor, and the anchor is the fixed AABB that stops twenty-one cells being twenty-one focal lengths. The heap is already capped; the cap is declared rather than absorbed by quietly growing the plate.

THE TOKEN NAME, FLAGGED RATHER THAN CHANGED. `assembly_stair` names one of the three objects this bench builds, and the stair is not privileged among them - it is one value of `object`. The name is the brief's and is kept so that the wave's manifests, the sweep slug and this registry agree; the axis is `assembly` and the artifact is about the word, not about stairs.
dna.sweep_note: THE FULL SHEET NEEDS --max=21 AND THE COST OF GETTING IT WRONG IS THE WHOLE SECOND HALF OF THE ARGUMENT. `assembly` is declared first and is never trimmed; `object` is second, and build_dna_gallery trims the LATER axis from the tail until the cross product fits its cap. At the default --max=9 the 7 x 3 sheet renders as 7 x 1 = `stair` only, which deletes all three designed nulls, the entire cross-object claim (the 43-percent-versus-zero contrast that IS the thesis) and the registered prediction, whose context is the table. It would leave a finished-looking sheet of seven tiles that cannot be wrong about anything. At --max=14 it renders 7 x 2 = stair and table, which restores the prediction and exactly ONE of the three nulls - and a single null cannot be checked against its own triangle. Only 21 carries the experiment.
